DATE : 6th APRIL 2026  ORAL JUDGMENT (Per Bharati Dangre, J.) :
1. Rule. Rule is made returnable forthwith with the consent of the parties and is taken up for final disposal.
Learned counsel appearing for the respondents waive notice on behalf of the respective respondents.

2. On 4th January 2020, the Food and Drugs Administration, Mumbai carried out raid in the godowns of the petitioner and seized 23-wpl.387.2023.doc huge quantity of product called "Amul Lite" and "Delicious."

Since the goods were seized, which allegedly were in contravention of the Food Safety and Standards Regulations which according to the petitioner were not yet finalized and had not yet come into force and therefore the seizure of the products according to the petitioner was unjustified.

3. When the petitioner approached this Court, he raised a challenge to the impugned action and sought release of the products with permission to market the same after repackaging them in conformity with the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

sentences.text: An alternative prayer was also sought that the seized products may be permitted to be sent back to the manufacturing unit for utilization as non-human consumption and as far as the product "Delicious." is concerned, it upon been blended @ 10% in the existing recipe, which would take care of the sub-standard parameters, it shall be packed in revised packaging material and then sold in the open market.

Apart from this, challenge was also raised to the amendment/modification under the Food Safety and Standards 23-wpl.387.2023.doc (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, by declaring that it is illegal, ultra vires and contrary to the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards 23-wpl.387.2023.doc (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: A declaration was also sought that the said Regulations of 2018 had not yet come into force on the date when the action was initiated against the petitioner and its goods came to be seized.

4. Upon the petition being filed, on 5 th November 2020, the Division Bench of this Court, taking note of the submissions advanced on behalf of the State Authorities, since it was indicated that it is going ahead with the auction, the goods being perishable in nature and State had already issued notices and tenders have been received, did not grant any interim relief.

However, as far as the prayer of the petitioner for initiating any coercive action, the order directed that if the respondents-authorities intend to take any coercive steps they will give 15 days advance notice to the petitioner.
The order also directed that any amount recovered through the sale conducted by the State Government will be subject to 23-wpl.387.2023.doc further orders to be passed in the petition.

5. The interim order granted to the aforesaid effect continued to remain in force and today when the writ petition is called up for hearing, learned counsel Mr. Khandeparkar made a categorical statement that he is not pressing for the challenge to the validity of the amended Regulation of 2018.

By inviting our attention to the affidavit-in-reply filed by the Assistant Commissioner (Foods) on behalf of respondent Nos.1 to 5, raising a preliminary objection that the petitioner had not availed any statutory remedy of Appeal available under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
and therefore the petition need not be entertained.

According to Mr. Khandeparkar, the said statement is incorrect and he has invited our attention to the Appeal Memo which is a part of the petition being annexed as Exhibit - 'T2' and 'T3' respectively, the Appeals being preferred under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, which is filed against the report of the analyst received on 25 th February 2020 and according to him, 23-wpl.387.2023.doc the Appeals are pending before the Designated Officer at Mumbai.

Mr. Khandeparkar make a statement that if the Appeals are directed to be decided within a time bound manner, as the product has now been analyzed and the report was submitted by the Food Analyst, but it had not yet attained finality in the wake of pendency of the Appeals, the petition would serve its purpose as the further course of action available to the petitioner as well as to the department would be only considered subsequent to the adjudication of the pending Appeals.
6.

We find substance in the said submission, as according to us, the report of the Food Analyst is subjected to a challenge to the Designated Office and once the petitioner has availed his remedy, and Gujarat Co-Operative Milk Marketing ... vs Adjudicating Officer/Joint ... on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183231633/

In any case the amount that is collected from the sale of the product is already safe in the State Treasury and the issue of disbursement of the amount to either of the parties shall 23-wpl.387.2023.doc also be dependent upon the final adjudication by Appellate Authority.

Since the Appeals are pending since 2020, we direct the Appellate Authority to pronounce upon the Appeals, which are annexed to the petition at Exhibit - 'T2 and 'T3' against the report of the Food Analyst, are directed to be decided by the Appellate Authority within a period of 12 weeks from today.
Needless to state, that for the purpose of hearing of the Appeals, if the presence of the petitioner is warranted, appropriate notice shall be issued and its representation shall be ensured.

However, till the Appeals are decided and for a further period of 7 weeks thereafter, we deem it appropriate to continue the interim order as regards any coercive action and if at all any coercive action is proposed, the safeguard of issuing 15 days notice shall be adhered to.
With the above directions, the writ petition is disposed of.
Rule is made absolute on the aforesaid terms.

MANJUSHA DESHPANDE, J. BHARATI DANGRE, J.
